summary: Follow-up to 2026-10-09-session-model-writer-spellings after PRs #150 to #157, #159, and #160 landed (there is no #158): older-generation migrations at any depth with a harness that deepens every shared case (#151), the undecided native limits settled (#152), owner decisions D28 and D29 and the rows they decide (#153, #154), Session directories named *.jsonl and the flat-layout refusal (#155), extra request config members (#156), lone surrogates held and written back as JSON.stringify does (#157), stored identity checked by realpath (#159), and the v2 codec recovery and migration traces (#160). The development-only bake-session and bake-cli crates are compared with TypeScript through 38 shared case tables (3529 cases) and three runtime captures. A clean checkout of candidate 5738aaba725899bffbfc79533c2f3c8c8d4afb2c passed 508 workspace Cargo tests (23 ignored by default), cargo fmt, clippy, and rustdoc, the ignored full deepened sweeps of bake-session and bake-cli, the 18 ignored million-level depth tests, and 4304 Vitest tests (7 skipped) in the 42 TypeScript specs that read those tables. CI for PR #160 tested synthetic merge a6fc9e38c2a0daff3a4a8f6fa38967efdb4ab4f9, which has the candidate's tree db758d2b5a46abcd7442d74936449eb4dda2eba8, and passed the native, runtime, and app-check jobs. One flipped shared-table expectation was rejected by both harnesses. The classification holds 107 limits: 99 unreachable, 7 reachable gaps, all accepted by owner decisions D26 and D28, and 1 undecided (cli-migration-limit, through zstd/stop-order); that limit, children's own logs, Agent resume, crash recovery, a Windows-host run of 35 of the specs, and full preflight are missing. Not scope acceptance.

results.behavior: All 42 TypeScript specs under packages/ that read a conformance/session or conformance/runtime table passed in 3.3 s: 4304 Vitest tests passed and 7 skipped (four win32-only lookup cases, limit-windows-name, which runs on Windows only, and identity-case-alias-written and identity-requested-id-case-alias, which run on case-insensitive macOS and Windows volumes, on this Linux host). Counts describe Vitest tests across 42 files, not table cases.

cargo test --workspace --locked passed 508 tests across 62 test targets (5 doc-test targets ran none) in 53.0 s, with 23 ignored by default. bake-session contributed 172: 74 unit tests and 98 integration tests in 39 binaries, with 20 ignored (17 million-level depth tests in deep_payload_cases, deepened_cases_full_sweep, its deepened_shard child, and the deepened_control child of deepened_negative_controls); bake-cli's 3 ignored are deepened_cli_full_sweep with its child and the million-level lookup test. Most integration tests iterate a whole shared table inside one test, so counts describe Cargo tests, not cases. The default deepened sweeps sample positions.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and rustdoc with -Dwarnings for bake-session and bake-cli exited 0. Each count is one command, not a test.

The ignored deepened_cases_full_sweep, which conformance/README.md describes as every position in both shapes (8,770 variants of 3,409 logs) through every public bake-session entry point on a small stack, passed in 170.6 s; the ignored deepened_cli_full_sweep, the same variants plain and Zstd-framed through bake-rs session inspect, inspect --root --id, stat, and list in-process, passed in 54.7 s. Each is one Cargo test that runs its shards in child processes; the logs print the pass, not the variant count. Durations are wall-clock on a 32-thread host with warm build caches, not a performance baseline.

All 17 ignored million-level tests in deep_payload_cases.rs passed in 223.5 s, among them migrations_a_million_deep and write_open_migrates_a_million_deep, which migrate plain and Zstd v0, v1, and v2 logs nested 1,000,000 levels; the ignored lookup_migrates_payloads_a_million_deep in session_lookup_deep.rs passed in 144.0 s. Counts describe Cargo tests.

docs/roadmap/rust-0.4/scope-02/native-limits.json (sha256 in the fixture manifest) classifies 107 native limits against D21, covering 316 limit cases in 33 tables: 99 unreachable (312 cases), 7 reachable gaps (4 cases), and 1 undecided. The reachable gaps are owner exceptions, not missing work: D28 accepts object-prototype-type and the five pass-through rows that carry it (v1-to-v2-decoded-payload, history-v0-to-v1, history-v1-to-v2-decoded, history-v2-to-v3, log-file-migration), and D26 accepts log-file-windows-name on a Win32 path platform; their rows name no follow-up. The undecided row is cli-migration-limit, a pass-through whose zstd/stop-order is untraced. rust/crates/bake-session/tests/native_limit_classification.rs, which passed 2 tests inside cargo-test, checks the classification against every limit variant and every native-limit expectation in the case tables. The check proves the table is complete and consistent, not that a classification is right.

Several tables carry explicit native-limit refusals that the Rust tests require instead of the TypeScript outcome. This checks refuse-rather-than-guess; it is not parity for those cases. Since the superseded record the migration depth bound is gone (D27: migrations read rows of any depth, witnessed by the million-level tests), the migration-row-json-parser, v2-codec-recovery, finish-order, lone-surrogate, legacy-layout, and identity limits were ported, and the undecided limits were settled or decided by D28 and D29, leaving only cli-migration-limit undecided.

On PR #160's synthetic merge a6fc9e38c2a0daff3a4a8f6fa38967efdb4ab4f9 (candidate tree), native preflight passed 5 gates on Linux and macOS (rust, rust-pty, rust-conformance, rust-eval, rust-lease) and 4 on Windows with rust-pty skipped (native ConPTY scenarios are not implemented). The rust gate runs check:rust, which includes cargo test without --ignored. Counts describe gates.

The rust jobs then ran seven of the 42 conformance specs (lookup, generation-header, stat, list, v2-to-v3 migration, subagent projection and catalog) on each OS: 850 passed and 4 skipped on Linux, 845 and 9 on macOS, 813 and 41 on Windows. Counts describe Vitest tests across those seven files.
The same run's runtime job passed the build, runtime (whole suite, since no merge base was found), and integration gates on Linux at the candidate tree. Counts describe gates.

App checks with --full --skip runtime,native passed 27 gates and skipped 9 on Linux, including typecheck, lint, verify-persistence-catalog, verify-rust-migration-inventory, the ledger verifier, tui-spec, and e2e; whitespace (no merge base), actionlint, and the seven runtime and native gates skipped by flag were the skips. Counts describe gates.

The windows-release job, which builds a release on a Windows host and runs ten runtime specs there, six of them shared-table conformance specs (header, log-scan, source-event-seqs, event-envelope, v3-row, and request-derivation).
